identity.title: SimuHome: A Temporal- and Environment-Aware Benchmark for Smart Home LLM Agents

problem.claim: Evaluate LLM agents for smart-home interaction under temporal environmental effects and scheduled device workflows.

gap.claim: Existing benchmarks model homes as static systems, omitting time-dependent environmental effects and workflow scheduling.

contributions.claim: Introduces SimuHome, a Matter-grounded high-fidelity smart-home simulator and 600-episode benchmark.
Covers state inquiry, implicit intent inference, explicit control, and workflow scheduling, including feasible and infeasible requests.
Reports workflow scheduling as the hardest category across 18 evaluated agents.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish SimuHome through temporal environmental simulation and immediate evaluation of scheduled workflows via time acceleration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that workflow scheduling is the hardest category among the evaluated tasks.
The authors report that failures in workflow scheduling persist across alternative agent frameworks and fine-tuning.
The authors suggest time-accelerated simulation can pre-validate agent actions before real-world execution.

narrative_sequence.summary: SimuHome is introduced as a 600-episode smart-home simulator and benchmark addressing static assumptions in existing benchmarks.
The simulator uses the Matter protocol, exposes APIs, models continuous temperature and humidity effects, and includes four task categories with feasible and infeasible requests.
Across 18 agents, workflow scheduling is reported as hardest, motivating simulation for pre-validation before real-world commitment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs task categories with both feasible and infeasible requests and reports scheduling failures across agent frameworks and fine-tuning.

lessons.interpretation: Separating capability coverage from feasibility handling can expose failure modes that aggregate success rates may hide.
lessons.application: When designing an agent benchmark, include valid and invalid requests within each task category and report failures by category and method variant.
lessons.exception: This structure may be unsuitable when invalid requests are outside the deployment contract or when the study targets only a narrowly defined valid-task capability.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide per-category scores, failure rates, agent identities, or evaluation protocols.
It does not specify the simulator's environmental dynamics, workflow horizon, or how closely simulation outcomes match real-device behavior.
